question: Ticket fc3859155412 says 'Find why the proof reds on Windows and fix it so the proof reseals green', but outline 9.4.2.3.7.6 reads "A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8)." (The outline prescribes two steps that the ticket's plan omits: (1) 'An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6' to determine whether code or tooth is wrong—the ticket just says 'find why' without specifying LLM involvement. (2) 'A tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion)'—the ticket fixes the test file (a tooth change) but does not specify the decision will be recorded in corrosion. If the ticket is built exactly as written (find and fix), without LLM determination and without decision recording, clause 9.4.2.3.7.6 does not hold.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
